body:
The visibility of a local business in Google results depends largely on the quality and completeness of its Google Business profile.

This free tool from Google allows any business to appear in Google Maps, in the local results pack and in the information panel on the right-hand side of the search page.

An optimized profile attracts new customers, generates phone calls and directs visitors to your website.

Many businesses create their Google Business profile and abandon it after filling in the basic information. This approach leaves a marketing channel with great potential untapped.

Google Business Profile: an optimization guide for local visibility


Optimizing your profile involves much more than adding your address and phone number. It requires an ongoing strategy for publishing content, managing reviews and using all the features the platform provides.

In this guide, you will learn how to optimize every section of your Google Business profile for maximum visibility in Google Maps, how to manage reviews to build trust and how to use advanced features that set you apart from competitors.

You will also discover common mistakes business owners make and the advanced strategies used by businesses that dominate local results.

Optimizing your Google Business profile is a core component of your local SEO strategy. Google's algorithm evaluates three main factors when ranking local results: relevance (how well your profile matches the search), distance (proximity to the user) and prominence (your business's recognition online). A complete and active profile positively influences all three factors.

Filling in the basic information


The first step is to make sure all your basic information is complete and correct. Google prioritizes complete profiles, and any missing information reduces your chances of appearing in relevant results.
Profile completeness is the first signal Google evaluates to decide whether your business is relevant to a particular search.
  • Business name: use the company's official name, exactly as it appears on documents. Do not add keywords or extra locations: Google penalizes this practice
  • Primary category: choose the category that best describes your main activity. This directly influences the searches you appear for
  • Secondary categories: add up to 9 additional categories for complementary services or products
  • Full address: include your exact address if you receive customers at your premises. For businesses that travel to customers, set the service area
  • Phone number: use a local number, not a toll-free or premium-rate number
  • Website: add the URL of your business's optimized website
  • Opening hours: set the correct hours for each day, including special holiday hours
Check the accuracy of your information regularly. Google may suggest changes based on information submitted by users, and if you do not review them, incorrect details may appear on your profile. Enable notifications in your Google Business account to be alerted whenever someone suggests a change to your profile.

Common mistakes when filling in basic information


Business owners often make mistakes that affect their visibility without realizing it. These are the most common problems and how to avoid them:
  • Adding keywords to the business name: a common practice, but one that can lead to profile suspension. If the business's real name is "Maria's Flower Shop", do not turn it into "Maria's Flower Shop: flower delivery Bucharest"
  • Inconsistent NAP information: Name, Address and Phone number (NAP) must be identical on your website, on Google Business and in every online directory where your business appears.
  • Categories that are too broad: if you run a dental clinic, do not select only "Medical services". Choose "Dental clinic" as your primary category
  • Outdated opening hours: profiles with incorrect hours receive negative reviews when customers arrive at the premises and find the business closed

Optimizing the business description


The business description allows up to 750 characters. Use this space strategically to communicate what your business offers and what sets it apart from competitors.
The description does not directly influence rankings in local results, but it persuades potential customers who reach your profile to contact your business.

Recommendations for the description:
  • Start with the most important information: your main services and area of operation
  • Include relevant keywords naturally: do not force keyword stuffing
  • Mention experience, certifications or elements that build E-E-A-T credibility
  • Use a professional tone that reflects your brand identity
  • Do not include links, phone numbers or promotions in the description: Google may reject it
  • Update the description at least once a year to reflect changes in your business activities
An example of an effective description for an accounting firm: "We offer accounting and tax consulting services for SMEs and medium-sized businesses in Bucharest, with over 15 years of experience. Our team of certified accountants ensures tax compliance, tax optimization and monthly financial reporting. Appointments available in person and online."

Photo and visual content strategy


Profiles with photos receive 42% more requests for directions in Google Maps and 35% more clicks to their website. Visual content is not optional. It is a major differentiator from competitors that neglect this component.

Types of photos you should add:

  • Business logo: a clear, square image that appears in search results
  • Cover photo: the main image representing your business, recommended size 1080 x 608 pixels
  • Interior and exterior photos: help customers recognize the location and feel comfortable before their first visit
  • Team photos: build trust and humanize the business
  • Product or service photos: show exactly what you offer
  • Photos of the work process: relevant for craftspeople, builders, restaurants and other businesses where the process matters
Add new photos regularly, at least 2-3 per month. Google interprets consistent activity as a signal of relevance. Optimize images according to SEO best practices before uploading: descriptive file names and optimized dimensions.
Avoid low-resolution photos, excessive filters or overlaid text.

Videos on Google Business


In addition to photos, you can upload videos up to 30 seconds long and 75 MB in size. Videos have an even greater impact than photos on profile visitor engagement.

Film a tour of your location, introduce your team or demonstrate a service. Make sure the videos are filmed at a minimum resolution of 720p and do not contain copyrighted music.

Managing reviews


Reviews are the factor with the greatest impact on customers' decisions and rankings in local results. A profile with many positive reviews and prompt responses from the business inspires trust in both users and Google's algorithm.

Studies show that 93% of consumers read online reviews before choosing a local business.

Effective review strategies:

  • Ask for reviews: ask satisfied customers to leave a review after the service is completed. Use the direct review link in the Google Business dashboard
  • Respond to every review: thank customers for positive reviews and address negative reviews constructively
  • Respond quickly: a response time of less than 24 hours shows that you pay attention to customer feedback
  • Personalize your responses: avoid generic, copied responses. Mention the customer's name and specific details
  • Create a short review link: from the Google Business dashboard, you can generate a short link to send to customers by SMS or email
Do not buy fake reviews or offer financial incentives for reviews. Google detects these practices and may penalize or suspend your profile. Build authentic reviews by consistently providing quality services.

How to respond to negative reviews


Negative reviews are inevitable for any business. How you respond to them is just as important as positive reviews. Follow this approach:
  1. Thank the customer for their feedback, regardless of the review's tone
  2. Acknowledge the problem without arguing with the customer in public
  3. Offer a specific solution or invite the customer to contact you directly
  4. Maintain a calm, professional tone in every situation
  5. Do not disclose the customer's personal information in your response
A good response to a negative review can turn a bad impression into a public demonstration of your professionalism.

Publishing posts on Google Business


Google Business allows you to publish posts similar to those on social media. These posts appear directly in the business profile in search results and have a lifespan of 7 days (except for offers and events with specific dates).
Regular posts signal to Google's algorithm that the business is active and relevant.

Available post types:
  • Updates: business information, tips or educational content
  • Offers: promotions with start and end dates and an optional coupon code
  • Events: event announcements with a date, time and description
  • Products: product presentations with a price and description
Publish at least one post per week to keep your profile active. Include a call-to-action button in every post: "Learn more", "Book", "Order online" or "Call now". Add a photo to each post. Posts with images generate more engagement than text-only posts.

Using the questions and answers feature


The questions and answers (Q&A) section in your Google Business profile allows anyone to ask questions about your business. If you do not actively monitor this section, other people may answer on your behalf with inaccurate or incomplete information.

This can cause confusion among potential customers and damage your business's reputation.

The recommended approach is to proactively create a set of frequently asked questions (FAQ) and answer them yourself. Useful questions include: opening hours, accepted payment options, whether an appointment is required, the returns policy and other information customers frequently request.

Monitor the Q&A section weekly. When someone adds a new question, respond as quickly as possible. You can mark your own answers as helpful by "liking" them to make them more visible.

Clear answers to frequently asked questions reduce the number of phone calls with simple questions and allow your team to focus on more valuable activities.

Advanced features for specific businesses


Google Business offers additional features depending on the type of business. These allow you to provide detailed information relevant to your category:
  • Online bookings: for restaurants, beauty salons, clinics and other appointment-based businesses, you can enable a booking button directly in your profile
  • Menu: restaurants and cafes can add their full menu with prices
  • Products and services: any type of business can list products and services with descriptions and prices
  • Attributes: specify whether your business is accessible to people with disabilities, whether you accept card payments, whether you offer free WiFi, etc.
  • Job openings: you can list available positions directly on your profile

Monitoring profile performance


Google Business provides detailed statistics about your profile's performance. Open the "Insights" section to see:
  • The number of profile views in Search and Maps
  • User actions: website clicks, phone calls, requests for directions
  • The searches through which users find your profile
  • The geographic areas that requests for directions come from
  • The number of photo views compared with similar profiles
Analyze these data monthly and adjust your strategy accordingly. If you notice that certain searches bring in a lot of traffic, create website content targeting those keywords to strengthen relevance. Connect Google Business data with Google Search Console for a complete picture of your online visibility.

Key performance indicators (KPI) for Google Business


Track these indicators monthly to measure optimization progress:
  1. Total number of actions: the sum of calls, website clicks and requests for directions per month
  2. Profile conversion rate: the percentage of profile visitors who take a specific action
  3. Growth in the number of reviews: how many new reviews you receive each month and changes in the average rating
  4. Number of direct vs. discovery searches: how many people search directly for the business name vs. generic searches such as "car repair in Cluj"
Optimizing your Google Business profile is an ongoing process that delivers cumulative results over time.

Every photo you add, every review you respond to and every post you publish helps increase visibility and trust in your business.

Apply the recommendations in this guide systematically, and you will see steady growth in the number of customers who discover you through Google.
